groups.subject_en: One Courage pip: a small ivory chess-piece BASE seen from above-front (a flat round plinth with a slight bevel and a tiny pawn-neck stub), the 'three small ivory chess bases'. The player has 3 pips, up to 5 with Courage Shards. Pips 4 and 5 are 'bonus' pips earned by shards and carry a thin crayon-blue rim so the player can tell shard Courage from base Courage.
groups.details_en: Bold readable silhouette at 1x on a dark HUD strip and on a light floor. 1 px charcoal outline, 2-tone ivory ramp, one pale-blue shadow pixel row. Same footprint in every file so they swap cleanly. Empty = the same plinth carved out as a dark felt socket with only the rim visible (no fill), NEVER red. The animated pop, gain and low-pulse effects are owned by the VFX lane; this group is only the resting states. The lost pip is a pip lost in this room: the empty socket with one hairline crack, shown while the pawn is invulnerable.
groups.avoid_en: Do not use red or coral anywhere (red is reserved for imminent damage). Do not draw a heart or a health bar.
groups.palette_en: ivory #F1E8D2 / shade #C9BFA6 / pale-blue shadow #AFC3DD / charcoal outline #2B2D3A / crayon blue rim #3A6FE0 on bonus pips
groups.notes_vi: Mỗi file là một ô Dũng khí (trạng thái tĩnh). Hiệu ứng nổ/hồi/nhấp nháy do lane VFX vẽ (courage_pip_pop, courage_pip_gain, courage_pip_low_pulse). Hiện game dùng health_pip 8x8, bản mới 16x16.
groups.used_in: HUD top-left Courage row; player damage; checkpoint refill; low Courage warning

groups.subject_en: The Rank label drawn as the CHILD's blue crayon tally marks, one file per Rank value 2..8. A tally is vertical strokes in groups of four with the fifth stroke a diagonal slash through them. Rank 2 = two strokes; Rank 5 = four strokes plus the slash; Rank 8 = four strokes + slash, then three more strokes. The marks are hand-drawn, slightly wobbly, with slightly different heights so it reads as a child's crayon, but they stay inside a clean 48x16 pixel grid.
groups.details_en: Stroke width 2 px, crayon-blue core with a 1 px lighter edge and a faint waxy break in the line (a missing pixel here and there). Stroke spacing 4 px. No outline box (the plate is a separate file). Rank is a story label, so the marks must look like a score kept by a child, not like a game level number.
groups.avoid_en: No digits, no word 'Rank' or 'Level'. Never use the word level look: no stars, no medal, no XP bar.
groups.palette_en: crayon blue #3A6FE0, lighter wax highlight #8FB2FF; the paper-coloured plate behind the tally is a separate file and is not drawn here
groups.notes_vi: Rank là nhãn cốt truyện, chỉ để đếm vạch. Vạch thứ 5 là nét chéo.

groups.anchor: bubble tail tip at (6,22); the bubble floats above the pawn's head
groups.subject_en: The silent pawn's emote bubbles (it never speaks): afraid, determined, relieved, glad, hesitant, calm, plus denied (the head-shake denial of an illegal chord) and ellipsis (waiting). Each is a small ivory speech bubble with a charcoal outline, a tail at the lower-left, and a single pictogram inside. Fired from drained events by presentation (afraid at low Courage, determined at a boss intro, relieved at boss defeat or a rescue, glad at a pickup or reunion, hesitant when the hand arrives, calm in the hub).
groups.details_en: Pictograms (no text): afraid = a sweat drop and a wavy mouth line in pale blue; determined = a bold forward chevron and a short brow line in warm ivory/charcoal; relieved = a soft exhale curl and a small sparkle; glad = a small upturned arc 'smile' with two sparkle dots in golden yellow; hesitant = three dots with the middle one raised; calm = a single small music-box note (the child's leitmotif); denied = a small head-shake mark: two horizontal swoosh ticks and a crossed arc; ellipsis = three evenly spaced dots. Each has a 2-px inner margin so it fits in the bubble.

groups.anchor: none (centred, the tile as the pack draws it)
groups.subject_en: The keyboard and gamepad glyphs of the control prompts, sourced (not drawn) from Kenney's CC0 pack 'Input Prompts Pixel'. The prompts and the Controls panel pick the glyph from the live InputMap, so every action shows the real bound key or button. Keys the input map uses: W A S D and the four arrow keys (move), Q (Pencil Thrust), F (Rule Step), G (Guard), R (call the child), E (interact), B (Book), K (alternate attack), C and V (skill slots 3 and 4, declared but unused), Space (attack, advance dialogue), Enter (advance dialogue), Shift (turn mode), Tab (next help page), Left Ctrl (focus), Left Alt (Free Step modifier), Esc (pause), F3 (debug overlay), F11 (fullscreen), plus blank caps for any other key. Gamepad inputs the input map uses: face buttons A B X Y, bumpers LB RB, triggers LT RT, stick clicks L3 R3, Start, Back, the D-pad and its four directions, the left and right stick, and the left-stick direction glyphs for move and for the Free Step diagonal cone. Connectors for multi-key prompts (plus, slash for 'or', right arrow for 'then', ellipsis), two device icons for the Controls tabs and an 'any key' glyph.
groups.details_en: Every tile of the pack is 16x16 pixels on a transparent background, drawn at 1 art pixel = 1 game pixel, so all 61 glyphs are 16x16 (the old 24x16, 32x16 and 48x16 wide-key sizes are gone: the prompt widget draws every key at 16x16). The pack ships a light and a dark style of each glyph; use the LIGHT tiles (the numbers named here) for every file so the whole set matches. Do not recolour, resize or smooth a tile. The gamepad glyphs use the pack's Xbox-style set as it is; the PlayStation and Switch sets of the same pack can be added later as extra files.
groups.avoid_en: redrawing or retouching a Kenney tile (except the quick edits a 'compose' line names), downloading from any page other than the pack page or its OpenGameArt mirror, adding the whole pack to the project, mixing light and dark styles inside the set, resizing a tile.
groups.palette_en: the pack's own colours; never recolour a tile
groups.notes_vi: Quyết định của anh (2026-10-12): dùng bộ Kenney CC0. Tải bộ 'Input Prompts Pixel' (800 tile 16x16, giấy phép CC0) từ kenney.nl/assets/input-prompts-pixel, giải nén vào thư mục mới ngoài project, rồi chép và đổi tên từng tile theo cột 'nguồn' của từng mục. Mức chắc chắn: tile = số tile đã đọc từ danh sách cộng đồng của đúng thư mục Tiles; locate = bộ có glyph nhưng chưa xác nhận số tile; compose = bộ không có, dùng tile thay thế hoặc bỏ trống. Mọi file có thể bị ghi đè bằng file vẽ tay cùng đường dẫn sau này. Đường dẫn giữ nguyên 61 file như UI mong đợi.
groups.used_in: PromptWidget, Controls panel, HUD slot hints

sourcing.download_en: Download the free ZIP from the pack page (about 330 KB, 800 PNG tiles of 16x16 pixels, version 1.0 of 2021; the OpenGameArt mirror https://opengameart.org/content/input-prompts-pixel-16%C3%97 carries the same files). Unzip it into a NEW empty folder outside the project, open its 'Tiles' folder (the tiles are numbered tile_0000.png upward) and copy only the tile named in SOURCE FILE IN THE PACK to the path in COPY AND RENAME TO; do not copy the whole pack into the project. sourcing.later_en: The pack is a long-term placeholder: any of these files can be replaced later by a hand-drawn 16x16 PNG saved at exactly the same path, and the game needs no change. Add 'Input Prompts Pixel, Kenney, CC0' to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (CC0 does not require credit; it is kind).

The Book of House Rules is the child's school exercise book: cream ruled paper, pale-blue rule lines, a pink margin line, a cardboard cover. It is the game's lore and loadout screen. groups.anchor: the corner point of the page sits at the bottom-right pixel (31,31) of the canvas
groups.subject_en: The page turn of the Book is a code tween, not 8 hand-drawn full-page frames: the engine scales the existing page panel (the right page, then the left page mirrored for the back of the leaf) around the spine edge. This file is the only piece of paper that is drawn for the turn: the lifted bottom-right corner of the leaf, curling up so the cream underside shows, drawn over the corner of the moving panel during the first half of the turn.
groups.details_en: A 32x32 right triangle of curled paper: a soft fold crease from the upper-right to the lower-left, the underside slightly darker than the page face, a 1 px charcoal outline #2B2D3A, hard pixel edges. The engine flips it horizontally for turns back.
groups.avoid_en: No text, no content on the leaf, no page numerals. No shadow baked in (the shadow is its own file), no glow.
groups.notes_vi: Thay cho 8 khung 272x304: chỉ vẽ góc giấy cong; phần lật là tween scale.x của panel trang có sẵn.

groups.anchor: none: tiles and stretches under the turning leaf
groups.subject_en: The soft shadow the turning leaf casts on the page below, built from two tiny reusable pieces that the engine tiles and stretches under the moving panel: a flat shadow tile and a stepped falloff edge. The shadow is a flat translucent fill (the one case where intermediate alpha is allowed), never a gradient.

groups.avoid_en: No text, no content on the leaf, no page numerals. No gradient, no feathered edge, no coloured shadow.

groups.subject_en: The Child: the human companion who plays the chess war. The child is shown mostly by a hand, a shadow and a voice, so the portrait is a 'child treatment': it is drawn the way the child draws themselves with wax crayons, a round face with a tuft of hair, two dot eyes, a simple mouth, bold wobbly outlines, scribbled fills in blue and warm skin tone, as a drawing on paper; it is NOT a realistic or photographic face. Lines are crayon-waxy (stippled fills with small gaps). The face is plain and sweet; hush = eyes lowered, mouth small and pressed, one hand drawn up near the mouth; afraid = wide dot eyes and a wavy mouth. Skin tone and hair are placeholder choices that the owner will set.
groups.details_en: 64x64 bust portrait on a transparent background, facing slightly toward the right, shoulders cut by the bottom edge; larger and more detailed than the in-game sprite, 1 px charcoal outline, 4-6 colours plus shading ramps. Emotion is carried by the eyes, brow, mouth and head tilt, with the same silhouette in every file so the engine can swap them with no layout jump. The emotion set is: neutral, glad, worried, afraid, hush (a quiet, lowered, held-back look), surprised.
groups.avoid_en: No speech tail. No weapon in front of the face. No red except hairline cracks on the Black King's own seams. Not the same expression in two files.
groups.palette_en: crayon blue #3A6FE0, warm skin placeholder #F0C8A0, yellow #F2C23C

groups.subject_en: The Child's hand: a small, soft child's right hand reaching into the chess world from outside the board, entering from the TOP-RIGHT of the screen (a child's hand in a blue-striped pyjama sleeve). It is the one thing in the game drawn far larger than a cell (this canvas is 192x144, because the hand is huge next to a pawn) and it uses the same 1x1 pixels as everything else, with many more of them: careful pixel work, soft ramps and a gentle selective outline. It must read as a real child's hand: short fingers, soft knuckle dimples, a slightly bitten-short fingernail, a thin wrist that disappears into a loose blue-striped sleeve cuff; the arm leaves the canvas through the top edge and the right edge. Motion is slower and heavier than the pawn's combat animation, with a hint of hesitation. The hand is NEVER a cursor, a glove, a divine beam or a glowing god-hand, and it does not glow.
groups.details_en: Canvas 192x144, transparent background. Anchor: the CONTACT POINT (where thumb and finger pinch a held object, or where the crayon tip touches the board) is at pixel (44,112) in EVERY frame, so frames swap without the contact point jumping; the forearm and sleeve leave the canvas through the top and right edges. Skin: a warm mid placeholder tone built from 4-5 ramp steps (shadow, base, light, highlight, rim) so the owner can recolour; a 1 px outline in a darker skin tone (not black) except where the hand meets the sleeve; sleeve = pale blue and white stripes (3 colours) with a soft cuff. No cast shadow in these files (the hand's shadow is a separate group). Held objects are NOT drawn in the hand (the Chalk Block, the pawn, the promotion tokens and the latch are separate props placed at the contact point), EXCEPT the blue crayon in the draw clip and the pink eraser in the erase clip, whose tips are the contact point. The pawn the hand holds is the separate sprite of the pawn hanging calm by its base (or the tilted, carried one while it is lifted), placed so its base-bottom centre is the contact point; the toppled pawn the hand lifts is a separate sprite lying flat at the contact point. The thumb and finger are drawn OVER the lowest 4 px of the pawn's base (the pawn is 22 px tall and smaller than its cell). Frames stay pixel-aligned (no subpixel blur), nearest-neighbour. Frames are authored for a hand entering from the top-right; the engine mirrors them horizontally when the target lies on the other side of the board.
groups.avoid_en: No cursor/pointer look, no glove, no glow or light beam, no cartoon white glove, no face, no extra fingers, no jewellery, no red sleeve, no cast shadow. Do not draw a held block, pawn, token or latch (separate props); only the crayon and the eraser are drawn in the hand.
groups.palette_en: skin placeholder: shadow #C98F63 / base #E8B88C / light #F5D3AE / highlight #FFE6C8, outline #8C5A3A; sleeve pale blue #AFC3DD / white #F2F4F8 / stripe blue #5A7EC0; crayon blue #3A6FE0 (draw clip only); eraser (erase clip only) desaturated pink #E8C6B8 (shade #C99F90), paper sleeve cream #EFE6CC
groups.notes_vi: Canvas 192x144 ≥ 160x120 theo plan. Ghi chú: 'gấp đôi mật độ pixel' nghĩa là nét vẽ mịn hơn thế giới cờ; nếu muốn đúng 2x thật thì vẽ 384x288 rồi scale 0.5 — hãy báo mình. Tay không phát sáng, không giống con trỏ. Phần plan: file hand_*.png được sửa thành thư mục anim/<clip>/NN.png. Clip erase (6 khung, M14, could) cho lời gọi Erase Rule Mark: bàn tay cầm cục tẩy hồng, vẽ luôn cục tẩy trong tay giống bút sáp của clip draw. Pawn bị nhấc/đặt dùng ảnh content/player/held_by_hand*.png, pawn nằm ngã dùng content/player/anim/defeat/06.png.

groups.title_vi: Font chữ pixel (khuyến nghị 1-2 font OFL có dấu tiếng Việt)
groups.subject_en: The pixel fonts for the game's UI, dialogue, Book and HUD numerals. THE OWNER SUPPLIES THE FILE; this group recommends OFL fonts (SIL Open Font License 1.1, free to embed and to credit in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Minimum on-screen glyph height is 10 px at 640x360 with extra line height for Vietnamese diacritics (the plan's D-25 leaves the source language to the owner, so Vietnamese coverage is the safe requirement). Checked on 2026-10-12 against the Google Fonts repository metadata (google/fonts, ofl/<font>/METADATA.pb): VT323 (OFL, subsets latin, latin-ext, vietnamese) is the recommended body font; Tiny5 (OFL, subsets include vietnamese, cyrillic, greek, latin-ext) is the recommended tiny font for HUD numerals and cooldown digits; Handjet (OFL, variable, subsets include vietnamese) is an optional headline/title-card font. For the child's lines, Patrick Hand (OFL, latin, latin-ext, vietnamese) or Shantell Sans (OFL, vietnamese, a marker-like hand) are hand-lettered options; the plan says the child uses a hand-lettered font only if the owner provides one.
groups.details_en: Do the real check before adopting a font, because the Google Fonts subset tag proves only that the subset is declared. The coverage check is automated: run `python3 tools/asset_requests/build_requests.py --check-font assets/fonts/ui_body_pixel.ttf` (or pass several font files, or point `--check-fonts <repo root>` at the project). The script reads the font's cmap table, the same table FontFile.has_char reads, and fails with a list of every missing code point out of the full Vietnamese set (all 134 precomposed letters including stacked marks such as ệ ẫ ờ ữ ặ, the base alphabet, digits and punctuation). The one step no script can judge stays with the owner: render the line-height and the diacritic clearance at the real sizes. Set Godot's font import to antialiasing none, hinting none/full and an integer size so pixel fonts stay crisp (VT323 is designed around a 16 px grid, so use 16 px or 32 px). Vector handwriting fonts (Patrick Hand, Shantell Sans) will not be pixel-crisp: keep them for the child's dialogue only, or let the owner hand-make a pixel handwriting font.
groups.avoid_en: Do NOT use Press Start 2P (no vietnamese subset) or Pixelify Sans (subsets are cyrillic, latin, latin-ext only; it lacks the vietnamese subset) if Vietnamese is shipped. Do not use a font whose licence is not OFL or CC0 without the owner's approval. Do not draw a font as images.
